Team,

When we started SwiftCart it was two of us, two scooters and a list of forty phone numbers. We promised thirty minutes because it sounded brave. Then we kept the promise, and people loved us for it, and we never once stopped to price it.

Six dark stores later, every new neighbourhood has added orders and cost in equal measure. The vans are full at the dinner rush and idle at three in the afternoon. We still owe the builder for the cold rooms. And the person who kept the numbers left, and we never replaced them.

You are not inheriting a failing company. You are inheriting a loved one that has never been run like a business. Don't be late. Our customers remember.

You inherit rails that work, merchants who trust us, and a promise that one day we would lend to the people the Bank turns away. Be careful who you let onto the rails, and careful what you promise.

Sign people. Stay safe. Get the licence.

Forgeline
Saturday 10 October 2026 · For every founder and member of staff of Forgeline · Reserve company: used only if it is in play

What your company knows at City Opens. New messages arrive in your company inbox during the day. Your live numbers are on the Company Station: if this dossier and the Station disagree, the Station is right.
At a glance

You run an idle factory with one customer. Forgeline is the only manufacturer among the companies, two companies say they cannot make their products without you, and your line runs at a third of what it can do. The machines are old, they eat Energy whether they work or not, and the order book has one name in it. If your group drew Forgeline as a new venture, read the last section first.
A letter from the founders
Team,

When the old owner left the city, the factory was going to be sold for scrap. We bought it instead, mostly out of stubbornness. The line still works. The machines are older than some of you, and they hum all day whether we use them or not.
We can make things here, inside a tick, at a fair price. We have proved it to exactly one customer. One customer is not a business. It is a favour waiting to end.
Systems beat heroics. Build the system: steady orders, steady materials, a line that never stands still.
The founders
Who you are
Your team
Your CEO is a volunteer playing the Operator: systems beat heroics; won't take orders the line can't fulfil; tends to avoid bold bets.

Your staff are strong in Operations: skilled line operators. You are one person short in Product / Build: nobody can adapt the line to a new product. That empty seat costs 225 VB every tick until it is filled. Everyone starts at Level 0 on 100 VB per tick.
Before Market Open, elect two Authorised Signatories. Either can approve spending up to 5,000 VB; above that needs the CEO or both together. Pick people who will be around at Tick 4.
Capital and resources

Figures assume a 9-person company; the platform sets your real numbers when registration closes. Your Company Station (the CEO volunteer's tablet) shows your live cash, stock, contracts, deadlines and people. Your Participant Portal (scan the QR on your badge) holds your wallet, offers and the deals you propose. There is no physical money: the platform is the record.
Products
A buyer without you pays an outside assembler 1,200 VB a batch plus 30 of its own Materials, and waits a tick. That is your sales pitch in one line.
What you start with: obligations
Customers and leads
Homeware Direct is your only steady income. It plans its shelves around your deliveries, so on time matters more to it than anything else.
Open customer cards sit at the Customer desk. Ask what each customer must have, and listen for what they need but did not write down.
Who you need, and who needs you

Others need you for manufacturing: a consumer brand and an energy company both say they cannot do without it, and new ventures need prototypes. That is leverage, and it is also exposure: if your line stops, they fall back to slower, dearer options. Decide early how hard you press them on price.
Immediate challenges
Bottleneck: Materials. Every run spends two more.
Weakness: no engineers to adapt the line.
Known risks: one customer, so losing it halves the order book; the old machines burn 3 extra Energy every tick; your Materials deal ends at Tick 4.
Objectives
Your CEO also holds a private objective in a sealed envelope, and each of you has a personal objective in your Portal.
Options on the table
Obvious: sell runs to businesses that cannot make their own products; sell spare line time to anyone, since it is the easiest yes in the building.
Worth finding: the produce supplier may have more bio-material than buyers; your first run for a new buyer is also your inspection batch.

Bigger moves: become a prototyping studio for the city's new ventures; launch an own-brand product line; be bought by a company that depends on you; merge with a produce supplier, from materials to finished goods.
What only you know

You also see what everyone plans to make before it reaches the market. None of these is marked true or false. You may share, sell or trade them. Some people on your team may hold a sealed note the rest have not seen. Ask.
Rules that matter most

A company is Distressed if its cash is below zero after a tick, it misses a loan payment, it has fewer than 3 staff, or a High or Very High resource sits at 0 for 2 ticks. You then have 2 ticks to fix it.
Stock: a warning at 30 units; at 15, anything using that resource costs 25% more of it; at 0, deliveries stop.
Your gate: a batch passes inspection when a run for any buyer other than your anchor is delivered in full, on the tick promised, and checked by the Customer desk.
Anyone may negotiate. A deal proposed in the Portal is real only when a signatory or the CEO accepts it.
Desks enter your purchases, loans, contracts and licences on the platform; check the Station afterwards.
Nothing settles before Tick 1. No outside internet or AI until the Internet Unlock at Tick 8.
Stuck on the platform? The helpdesk is open all day.
If your group drew this company as a new venture

Once the GM opens the Founder Window, 3 or more people can found a company with 10,000 VB committed between you from wallets or resources, plus a recorded founder agreement and resource agreement. You drew Forgeline at random and run it yourselves: there is no volunteer CEO. You must record a sale or a customer contract within 2 ticks, or Forgeline becomes Distressed. Each person can found only once, and only a limited number of new companies can start in a day, first come first served. Your GM's start sheet replaces the cash, resources, anchor, supplier deal and technical debt above, and tells you where to read your Company Station. Everything else here still describes your company. Spare line time is your quickest first sale.
